title: Run-length codec with validation
prompt:
A run-length code works on texts made of lowercase letters `a` to `z`, the dot `.` and the tilde `~`. To encode a text, split it into maximal runs of one repeated character (a run is n copies of a character c, as long as possible) and write each run, in order:
- a run of `~` (of any length n) is written as `~`, then n in decimal, then `~`;
- a run of any other character with n of 4 or more is written as `~`, then n in decimal, then c;
- any other run is written as it is (c repeated n times).
For example, `aaaaab~` is encoded as `~5ab~1~`.
To decode a code, read it from left to right. A `~` must be followed by a count (one or more decimal digits, the first of which is not 0) and then one more character c, which must be a lowercase letter, `.` or `~`; together they stand for c repeated count times. Any other character stands for itself, and must be a lowercase letter or `.`. A code that breaks any of these rules is invalid (for example a code that ends right after `~` or right after a count).
First encode each of these texts, in this order, and print one line per text in the form `encode TEXT -> CODE`: `aaaabbbcccccd`, `~~x`, `.......` (seven dots), `abc`, `zzzzzzzzzzzzzz~` (fourteen z and one tilde), `a~~~~b`.
Then decode each of these codes, in this order, and print one line per code: `decode CODE -> TEXT` if the code is valid and encoding TEXT gives exactly CODE again; `decode CODE -> TEXT (non-canonical)` if the code is valid but encoding TEXT gives a different code; `decode CODE -> invalid` if the code is invalid. The codes: `~4a~3~b`, `~04a`, `~2ab`, `a~b`, `~12z`, `~5`, `ab~3~~`, `x~1~y`, `q7`, `~10.~4~`, `~1~~1~`, `a~3B`.
expected_output:
encode aaaabbbcccccd -> ~4abbb~5cd
encode ~~x -> ~2~x
encode ....... -> ~7.
encode abc -> abc
encode zzzzzzzzzzzzzz~ -> ~14z~1~
encode a~~~~b -> a~4~b
decode ~4a~3~b -> aaaa~~~b
decode ~04a -> invalid
decode ~2ab -> aab (non-canonical)
decode a~b -> invalid
decode ~12z -> zzzzzzzzzzzz
decode ~5 -> invalid
decode ab~3~~ -> invalid
decode x~1~y -> x~y
decode q7 -> invalid
decode ~10.~4~ -> ..........~~~~
decode ~1~~1~ -> ~~ (non-canonical)
decode a~3B -> invalid
